claim: Chronic alcohol misuse promotes hyperalgesia.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In adolescents, untreated pain correlates with earlier initiation of alcohol use.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The prelimbic (PrL) subregion of the mPFC receives inputs from the basolateral amygdala (BLA).
source: The prelimbic (PrL) subregion of the mPFC receives inputs from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) (Cunningham et al., 2002; Gabbott et al., 2006; Krettek and Price, 1977) and sends projections to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) (An et al., 1998; Floyd et al., 2000), both regions involved in nociception.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The prelimbic (PrL) subregion of the mPFC sends projections to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG).

claim: Glutamatergic inputs from the BLA drive parvalbumin interneuron (PVIN)-mediated feedforward inhibition of pyramidal neurons projecting from the PrL to the vlPAG to promote nociception.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Activation of PrL PVINs is pronociceptive.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: AIE significantly reduced paw withdrawal threshold, indicating increased sensitivity to mechanical touch.
source: For mechanical sensitivity, analysis of data from the electronic Von Frey test revealed that AIE significantly reduced paw withdrawal threshold, indicating increased sensitivity to mechanical touch (main effect of AIE: F(1,115) = 12.81, p = 0.0005, partial η2 = 0.1002 [0.0203, 0.2105]; Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the behavioral experiments with statistical support and reference to Figure 1A, B.

claim: Female rats exhibited greater sensitivity to mechanical touch compared to male rats.
source: Additionally, female rats exhibited greater sensitivity to mechanical touch compared to male rats (main effect of sex: F(1,115) = 5.98, p = 0.0160, partial η2 = 0.0494 [0.0014, 0.1434]).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: There was no significant interaction between AIE and sex on mechanical touch sensitivity.
source: There was no significant interaction between AIE and sex (AIE × sex interaction: F(1,115) = 1.02, p = 0.3147).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Mechanical touch sensitivity decreased with age.
source: Mechanical touch sensitivity decreased with age (main effect of age: F(8,920) = 75.08, p = 0.0000, partial η2 = 0.3950 [0.3444, 0.4328]), with no significant interactions between age and AIE or sex (AIE × age interaction: F(8,920) = 0.70, p = 0.6327; sex × age interaction: F(8,920) = 1.50, p = 0.1829; AIE × sex × age interaction: F(8,920) = 1.10, p = 0.3602).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: AIE exposure did not significantly alter thermal sensitivity.
source: For thermal sensitivity, analysis of data from the Hargreaves test indicated no significant effect of AIE on paw withdrawal latency (main effect of AIE: F(1,115) = 1.21, p = 0.2738; Figure 1D, E).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments with reference to Figure 1D, E.

claim: There were no significant sex differences in thermal sensitivity.
source: Additionally, there were no significant sex differences or interactions with AIE (main effect of sex: F(1,115) = 0.59, p = 0.4446; AIE × sex interaction: F(1,115) = 1.85, p = 0.1767).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Thermal sensitivity decreased with age.
source: Thermal sensitivity was found to decrease with age (main effect of age: F(8,920) = 11.45, p = 0.0000, partial η2 = 0.0906 [0.0520, 0.1197]).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: AIE-driven reductions in paw withdrawal threshold persisted for more than 8 weeks after discontinuing ethanol vapor exposure.

evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Carrageenan induced an increase in mechanical sensitivity.

evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments with reference to Figure 2C-F.

claim: Female rats displayed a greater increase in mechanical sensitivity than males across both the saline and carrageenan treatments.
source: Analysis further indicated that female rats displayed a greater increase in sensitivity than males across both the saline and carrageenan treatments, with no significant effects of AIE, or interactions between AIE, sex, and carrageenan (main effect of sex: F(1,105) = 6.22, p = 0.0142, partial η2 = 0.0559 [0.0020, 0.1578]; main effect of AIE: F(1,105) = 0.93, p = 0.3366; AIE × sex interaction: F(1,105) = 0.03, p = 0.8706; AIE × carrageenan interaction: F(1,105) = 0.59, p = 0.4441; sex × carrageenan interaction: F(1,105) = 1.72, p = 0.1925; AIE × sex × carrageenan interaction: F(1,105) = 1.18, p = 0.2790).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Carrageenan induced an increase in thermal sensitivity.

claim: AIE and carrageenan enhanced the intrinsic excitability of PrLPAG neurons.

evidence: This is a statistical finding from the electrophysiological experiments with reference to Figure 4A-G.

claim: The effect of AIE on intrinsic excitability of PrLPAG neurons became more pronounced with increasing current step size.
source: Moreover, the effect of AIE on intrinsic excitability became more pronounced with increasing current step size (AIE × current step interaction: F(20,1440) = 3.82, p = 0.0117, partial η2 = 0.0503 [0.0194, 0.0604]).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the electrophysiological experiments.

claim: Carrageenan reduced the AP threshold of PrLPAG neurons, with the largest reduction observed in AIE exposed rats.

claim: There were no significant effects of treatment condition or sex on rheobase in PrLPAG neurons.

claim: Hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih) linked voltage sag was reduced by carrageenan in PrLPAG neurons.

claim: AIE reduced the E/I ratio at PrL PVINs, with a more pronounced reduction observed in males than in females.

evidence: This is a finding from the study that is consistent with prior research cited.

claim: Carrageenan is a well-known proinflammatory agent that induces edema and transient hyperalgesia in the carrageenan-induced inflammatory paw pain model.
source: Carrageenan is a well-known proinflammatory agent that induces edema and transient hyperalgesia in the carrageenan-induced inflammatory paw pain model (Benitz and Hall, 1959; Neves et al., 2020; Vazquez et al., 2015; Winter et al., 1962; Yang and Tsaur, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: AIE may selectively strengthen the input from PrLPAG neurons onto vlPAG GABA neurons, resulting in mechanical allodynia.
source: While speculative, we hypothesize that AIE selectively strengthens the input from PrLPAG neurons onto vlPAG GABA neurons, resulting in mechanical allodynia that could be alleviated by inhibiting PrLPAG neurons or activating PrL PVINs.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a speculative hypothesis by the authors.

source: Intrinsic excitability is also enhanced in PrL pyramidal neurons 3–5 days after intraplantar injection with complete Freund's adjuvant (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In a kaolin-carrageenan arthritis model, the amplitude of BLA-driven electrically evoked IPSCs (eIPSCs) onto PrL pyramidal neurons is significantly increased without a corresponding change in glutamate transmission.
source: These findings are similar to those seen in a kaolin-carrageenan arthritis model, where the amplitude of BLA-driven electrically evoked IPSCs (eIPSCs) onto PrL pyramidal neurons is significantly increased without a corresponding change in glutamate transmission (Ji et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Enhanced inhibitory transmission at PrL pyramidal neurons is a hallmark of carrageenan-induced inflammatory pain.
source: These findings indicate that enhanced inhibitory transmission at PrL pyramidal neurons is a hallmark of carrageenan-induced inflammatory pain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings of the study and comparison with prior research.

claim: AIE augments the number of perineuronal net (PNN) enwrapped PVINs in the PrL cortex.
source: Intriguingly, AIE augments the number of perineuronal net (PNN) enwrapped PVINs in the PrL cortex (Dannenhoffer et al., 2022; Obray et al., 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PNNs play a role in stabilizing synapses and restricting plasticity.
source: As PNNs play a role in stabilizing synapses and restricting plasticity (Cornez et al., 2020; Pizzorusso et al., 2002), this may reduce synaptic plasticity at PrL PVINs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: AIE-induced alterations in BLA–PrL–vlPAG function may impact other PrLPAG neuron-mediated behaviors such as context fear discrimination, passive avoidance, and arousal.
source: Beyond the implications for nociception, these AIE-induced alterations in BLA–PrL–vlPAG function may impact other PrLPAG neuron-mediated behaviors such as context fear discrimination (Rozeske et al., 2018), passive avoidance (Johnson et al., 2022), and arousal (Guo et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential broader implications, supported by citations to prior research on these behaviors.

claim: PrLPAG neurons project to both GABA and glutamate neurons in the vlPAG.
source: As PrLPAG neurons project to both GABA and glutamate neurons in the vlPAG (Guo et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2019), and these populations have been shown to be pro- and antinociceptive, respectively (Samineni et al., 2017), the balance of PrLPAG input onto these populations may determine the effect of PrLPAG activation on nociception.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: GABA and glutamate neurons in the vlPAG have been shown to be pro- and antinociceptive, respectively.
source: As PrLPAG neurons project to both GABA and glutamate neurons in the vlPAG (Guo et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2019), and these populations have been shown to be pro- and antinociceptive, respectively (Samineni et al., 2017), the balance of PrLPAG input onto these populations may determine the effect of PrLPAG activation on nociception.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The balance of PrLPAG input onto GABA and glutamate neurons in the vlPAG may determine the effect of PrLPAG activation on nociception.

evidence: This is a logical inference based on the cited research about the projections and functions of these neuronal populations.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in the PrL cortex can be classified as intratelencephalic (IT) or extratelencephalic (ET) based on their projection targets.
source: As pyramidal neurons in the PrL cortex can be classified as intratelencephalic (IT) or extratelencephalic (ET) based on their projection targets (Anastasiades and Carter, 2021; Baker et al., 2018a) and as each of these populations display unique physiological properties (Baker et al., 2018b; Dembrow et al., 2010), one potential explanation for these results is that adolescent ethanol exposure differentially effects these populations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: IT and ET pyramidal neuron populations display unique physiological properties.
source: As pyramidal neurons in the PrL cortex can be classified as intratelencephalic (IT) or extratelencephalic (ET) based on their projection targets (Anastasiades and Carter, 2021; Baker et al., 2018a) and as each of these populations display unique physiological properties (Baker et al., 2018b; Dembrow et al., 2010), one potential explanation for these results is that adolescent ethanol exposure differentially effects these populations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Adolescent ethanol exposure may differentially affect IT and ET pyramidal neuron populations.
source: As pyramidal neurons in the PrL cortex can be classified as intratelencephalic (IT) or extratelencephalic (ET) based on their projection targets (Anastasiades and Carter, 2021; Baker et al., 2018a) and as each of these populations display unique physiological properties (Baker et al., 2018b; Dembrow et al., 2010), one potential explanation for these results is that adolescent ethanol exposure differentially effects these populations.
evidence: This is presented as a potential explanation for the observed results.

claim: IT pyramidal neurons projecting from the PrL to the BLA and the nucleus accumbens do not display altered intrinsic excitability following AIE exposure.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, IT pyramidal neurons projecting from the PrL to the BLA and the nucleus accumbens do not display altered intrinsic excitability following AIE exposure (Obray et al., 2022) whereas PT PrLPAG neurons do.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PT neurons display greater Ih-dependent voltage sag than IT neurons.
source: Notably, PT neurons display greater Ih-dependent voltage sag than IT neurons, and adolescent alcohol exposure has been reported to reduce Ih current (Salling et al., 2018), suggesting a possible mechanism for greater ethanol effects on intrinsic excitability in ET neurons than in IT neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Adolescent alcohol exposure has been reported to reduce Ih current.
source: Notably, PT neurons display greater Ih-dependent voltage sag than IT neurons, and adolescent alcohol exposure has been reported to reduce Ih current (Salling et al., 2018), suggesting a possible mechanism for greater ethanol effects on intrinsic excitability in ET neurons than in IT neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PVIN intrinsic excitability is developmentally regulated and increases during adolescence.
source: Notably, PVIN intrinsic excitability is developmentally regulated and increases during adolescence (Koppensteiner et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Voluntary alcohol consumption during adolescence elicits sex-dependent effects on PrL somatostatin interneuron intrinsic excitability.
source: Intriguingly, voluntary alcohol consumption during adolescence elicits sex-dependent effects on PrL somatostatin interneuron intrinsic excitability (Sicher et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Somatostatin neurons receive inputs from the BLA and project to PrL PVINs.
source: As these neurons receive inputs from the BLA (Cummings and Clem, 2020; McGarry and Carter, 2016) and project to PrL PVINs (Cummings and Clem, 2020), it is possible that somatostatin neurons are responsible for the sex-dependent effects of AIE on E/I balance and oIPSCs at PVINs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Somatostatin neurons may be responsible for the sex-dependent effects of AIE on E/I balance and oIPSCs at PVINs.
source: As these neurons receive inputs from the BLA (Cummings and Clem, 2020; McGarry and Carter, 2016) and project to PrL PVINs (Cummings and Clem, 2020), it is possible that somatostatin neurons are responsible for the sex-dependent effects of AIE on E/I balance and oIPSCs at PVINs.

source: Notably, chronic activation of a PrL nociceptive ensemble including PrLPAG neurons has been shown to induce chronic pain-like behaviors (Qi et al., 2022).

source: While changes within the extended amygdala circuitry contribute to altered nociception in AIE exposed animals (Bertagna et al., 2024; Kelley et al., 2024; Secci et al., 2024), the impact on prefrontal nociceptive circuits remains unexplored.
